content.title: About
content.content: Baby arugula (Arugula, Eruca vesicaria) is a leafy vegetable with a distinctive peppery, slightly bitter flavor. It belongs to the Brassicaceae family and is commonly used in salads, garnishes, and as an aromatic addition to many dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Arugula is known as “rocket”, “rucola”, and “roquette” in different regions.
In ancient Rome, arugula was used as a medicinal herb to aid digestion.
The pungent glucosinolates that give arugula its taste also help deter certain garden pests.
Young leaves are harvested within the first 30‑40 days of growth, when they are most tender and flavorful.
Arugula thrives in cool climates and is often considered a “winter” salad green.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains vitamin A and carotenoids
items.content: Support vision, immune function, and skin health.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is needed for DNA synthesis and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Low‑calorie source of fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Glucosinolates and polyphenols help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to cruciferous vegetables.

items.title: Interaction with anticoagulants
items.content: High vitamin K content can reduce the effectiveness of blood‑thinning medications.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Arugula contains modest amounts of oxalates, which may be a concern for people prone to kidney stones.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat baby arugula raw in salads, add it to sandwiches, pastas, or pizza after baking, or blend it into smoothies. For a milder taste, lightly sauté it with olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store arugula in the refrigerator in a bag with a small amount of moisture or in a container lined with a paper towel. Use within 3‑5 days and discard wilted leaves.
